statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PENDING RETIREMENT
statements.title: PENDING RETIREMENT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today because I have heard from many of my constituents whose Federal retirement benefits are still delayed.

Mr. Speaker, I call on this administration to honor the commitment we made to civil servants and process these retirements expeditiously. using flock cameras for warrantless searches Mr. Speaker, imagine if someone followed you around everywhere you went with a notepad logging every single one of your moves, everywhere you went, and everything you did, and then reported that to a private company that sells that data to law enforcement or to the highest bidder.
More than 50 law enforcement officers have been accused or charged with misusing this technology, and we cannot continue to let this stand.

There are commonsense ways that security researchers, industry experts, and even Members of Congress here agree can make this safer, like auditing, information reporting, transparency, building safety throughout the AI development process, and real containment strategies, so that AI models don't escape their sandbox during development.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: REBUILDING USAID
statements.title: REBUILDING USAID
sentences: Mr. Speaker, when the Trump administration slashed USAID funding and fired its dedicated employees, they said it was a crowning achievement of fiscal responsibility because why spend money abroad, spend it on everyday Americans instead.
They gave tax cuts to the wealthiest corporations and cut Americans' health benefits and food assistance instead.
Because of the cuts to USAID, we are now seeing how it actually puts American lives and American dollars at massive risk.

If you think foreign aid doesn't affect you, let's look at the most recent example, because more than 70 Americans, including 9 Virginians, some in my district, are missing right now in Nepal because of the catastrophic floods that happened there last week.

USAID was running a natural hazards program to monitor and identify landslides, disasters, and climate events in Nepal and the project's former director said that the cuts to that program undermined ``landslide situational awareness.'' Imagine how many lives, and yes, even how much money we could have saved, and all the damage we could have prevented.
USAID was America's frontline defense against global chaos by building peace, providing clean water, and stabilizing unstable regions.
In fact, Jim Mattis, Trump's old Secretary of Defense said: ``If we don't fund the State Department fully, then I need to buy more ammunition ultimately.'' Let's refund USAID.

That is why we should be debating a real stock trading ban like the Restore Trust in Government Act, one that would ban Members of Congress, the administration, and their families from owning, buying, or selling individual stocks.
Instead, House Republicans only allow us to vote on a toothless, watered-down stock trading bill.
Plus, to make sure that this fake stock trading ban doesn't move in the Senate, they throw in the SAVE America Act, which would disenfranchise millions of Americans.
I ask: Why are we afraid to put a comprehensive stock trading ban on the floor and have it apply to the President, too?
Let's vote on a real stock trading ban and vote ``no'' on this fake ban with voter suppression.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SURVEILLANCE PRICING
statements.title: SURVEILLANCE PRICING
sentences: Surveillance pricing feeds your personal information and your online activity into an algorithm.
That algorithm then raises the price you see online for your purchase based on how much it thinks it can get away with charging you.

If the algorithm recognizes, based on your web search history, that a family member just passed away and you need to fly across the country, with surveillance pricing, the airline can then use that information to jack up the price of your flight.
It is like personalized price gouging.
This bill requires businesses to disclose the use of surveillance pricing and requires that consumers are able to opt out of surveillance pricing.
Customers have the right to know if their personal data is being used to force them to pay unfair prices.
I urge my colleagues to join me in lowering costs by putting an end to online price gouging and predatory surveillance pricing.
Data Center Overview Mr. Speaker, there are over 5,000 data centers in this country, with thousands more planned.
Data centers could use 12 percent of the entire country's energy by 2028.
This can lead to irresponsible data center build-outs, electric grid instability, and high energy prices.
Americans deserve to know how much energy and water data centers actually are using and not just estimates.
This bill will establish consistent and accurate measures for how much water and energy are used by data centers.
With this transparent information, communities will be able to decide if they want to host a data center.
Energy infrastructure can be properly planned, away from homes and schools, and we can understand, finally, data centers' full impact on our communities.
I urge my colleagues to join me in passing this legislation so that Americans are not left guessing when it comes to data centers.
Need for Gun Safety Legislation Mr. Speaker, every day nearly 130 people are killed from gun violence.
Far too many families, far too many friends, and far too many loved ones have to cope with a devastating loss because of gun violence.
June marks Gun Violence Awareness Month.

My first bill, the Gun Safety Innovation Opportunity Act, supports research into cutting-edge gun safety technologies, like using fingerprints to ensure that only authorized users can access that firearm.
That is why I am introducing the Protect Every Preschooler Act, legislation to extend existing gun safety protections to our youngest learners at preschools and early childhood education campuses.
I urge my colleagues to join me in supporting these bills and renewing our commitment to keeping all of our communities safe from gun violence.
That is why I am introducing the SLASH Prices Act.
That is why I am introducing the bipartisan Data Infrastructure Energy Measurement and Standards Act.
I am proud to introduce commonsense measures to promote firearm safety and prevent more of these deaths.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TESTIMONY OF SKY AND AMANDA ROBERTS, "SURVIVORS FIGHT FOR JUSTICE: EXPOSING EPSTEIN'S CRIMES IN PALM BEACH AND ACROSS THE WORLD"
statements.title: TESTIMONY OF SKY AND AMANDA ROBERTS, "SURVIVORS FIGHT FOR JUSTICE: EXPOSING EPSTEIN'S CRIMES IN PALM BEACH AND ACROSS THE WORLD"
sentences: Mr. Speaker, on May 12, 2026, Oversight Committee Democrats convened the first-ever hearing to solicit testimony from survivors of Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell's crimes.
The hearing, ``Survivors Fight for Justice: Exposing Epstein's Crimes in Palm Beach and Across the World,'' marked a critical step forward in the fight for justice and accountability.

On behalf of all the survivors of Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell's crimes, I rise to include in the Record the testimony offered by Sky and Amanda Roberts: My name is Sky Roberts, and I am the little brother of Virginia Roberts Giuffre.

First, I want to thank this committee, Representative Garcia, and everyone who continues to fight for accountability, transparency, and truth in the Epstein case and most importantly, for standing with survivors.
Epstein and Maxwell did not act alone.
Virginia wrote in Nobody's Girl ``Don't be fooled by those in Epstein's circle who said they didn't know what Epstein was doing.'' That sentence should guide this committee's work.
When people like Les Wexner are asked about Epstein's finances and alleged connections to this network, the public deserves real answers.
When Howard Lutnick has given changing accounts about his association with Epstein, that deserves scrutiny and resignations.
And finally: The Epstein and Maxwell investigations must be reopened.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FUND THESE GRANTS
statements.title: FUND THESE GRANTS
sentences: Protecting Data Centers Mr. Speaker, data centers hold critical information we use every day and keep the internet running.
Whether it is AI, blockchain, or any other innovations in technology, data centers are going to be a key part of this.
Because data centers are so critical, they are becoming targets during wars.
Look at the Russian-Ukrainian war.
Russia is attacking Ukrainian data centers.
Iran has struck commercial data centers in the UAE and has said that data centers are military targets now.
My district is home to hundreds of data centers, and families, schools, parks, and places of worship are all close to data centers in my district.
People living around these data centers shouldn't have to worry about being a target anymore.
This bill would direct the Department of Homeland Security to develop a strategy to protect data centers and the communities around them from being targeted during attacks.

The government needs to do everything possible to protect these communities because Americans deserve to know that if a data center is going to be built next to them, we will protect that community, and they won't be a target at that point.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to call out the rise we are seeing in hateful rhetoric.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: RESTORING ELECTION INTEGRITY
statements.title: RESTORING ELECTION INTEGRITY
sentences: Mr. Speaker, today marks 16 years since the Supreme Court's disastrous decision in Citizens United.
The decision overturned critically important limits on political spending by corporations and billionaires.
We said it at the time, and it has come true: The decision has unleashed unprecedented spending by dark money groups on our elections.
Now campaigns are often defined not by a candidate's record or their ideas but, rather, by their access to dark money.
The wealthiest individuals and corporations can now help skew elections singlehandedly by giving millions to their preferred candidate.
Super-PACs spent $4.5 billion.
In the 2024 Presidential election, the biggest super-PACs supporting majority party nominees raked in $865 million from donors who contributed $5 million or more alone.
Between 2010 and 2024, the percentage of Federal election spending by the top 100 individual donors has jumped from 2 percent to almost 15 percent.
Yet, after Citizens United, it is too often small groups of corporations and billionaires tipping the scales based on who serves their business interests.
We must limit super-PACs, dark money, and excessive campaign spending.
We must restore democracy to the way our Founders intended, centered on equal access to government, and we must overturn Citizens United.
Mr. Speaker, there are a lot of reforms that people have proposed to overturn the damage done by Citizens United.
One of the things that Citizens United did was make it easier for foreign nationals to funnel money into U.S. elections.
The Federal Election Campaign Act currently prohibits foreign nationals from contributing to U.S. elections and political campaigns.
However, it does not prohibit Americans from assisting foreign nationals from seeking to do so.
It is a small tweak, but my bill will prohibit Americans from assisting foreign nationals who want to contribute to U.S. elections.
For now, this is a step in the right direction as we all work toward the larger goal of overturning Citizens United.
Working families are struggling with rising expenses, like healthcare, housing and utilities, and groceries, yet they have representation that seems to reflect the very wealthiest.
We just passed a tax cut for the very wealthiest Americans this last summer, and people don't understand why.
If you look back at what happened with Citizens United, you realize that that influence on our campaigns and elections is why you end up with policies like that.
This is why we have to make sure that we overturn Citizens United.
It is the cycle and the concentration of wealth because of Citizens United that has led to the concentration of political power that you can see even more concentration of wealth.
It is the cycle that Citizens United has created that is hurting our country and leading to record income inequality.

While the long-term goal is to overturn Citizens United, certainly through a constitutional amendment--that is a very difficult goal, but certainly one that we should aspire to--Congress does have the power to act immediately to curb some of its damage.
We are talking about bills like the Freedom to Vote Act, the DISCLOSE Act, the Protecting Our Democracy Act, and the Ban Corporate PACs Act.

If you just look back at the past couple of decades since Citizens United, since 2010--in 2010, in that cycle, $3.6 billion in total cost of Federal elections by election cycle, then it goes up to $6.3 billion.
By 2024 it is at $15.9 billion.
Again, all of that is because of Citizens United and because of the ability to just flood these PACs, these super-PACS, dark money super-PACs, with as much money as they want with no accountability.
This is the 16th anniversary of Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission.

This decision overturned longstanding precedent that we had in this country, where we had clearly established limits on independent political spending by corporations and billionaires, and it was working.

Sometimes, it had gone down when it comes to the contributions of billionaires and the largest corporations, and we were able to have an election system where there was a lot of money in the system, but not to where we are today, where it has completely engulfed all of our actions and all of our campaigns.
There has been so much damage caused by Citizens United, as many of my colleagues explained today.
A lot of times, it is very easy to hide your contributions to these PACs and super-PACs.
That is why I felt the need to even try to address the influence of foreign money, because it has become easier than ever for a foreign entity to also infiltrate our elections.

We are talking about our efforts to lower prescription drug costs and healthcare costs, and how we see all the money spent by some of those groups to prevent legislation that will help the American people.
My colleague from New Mexico talked about the influence of oil and gas and that money on trying to address the environment--clean air, clean water, and climate change.

We are talking about efforts that we are trying to make to crack down on corporate price gouging and how it has become incredibly difficult, an almost uphill battle when it comes to some price gouging efforts, because of the influence of all of this money on our politics.
I have been through it, and I know many of our colleagues have been through it, where these super-PACs come in and change the dynamics of an election with millions and millions of dollars.
Again, I go back to the Freedom to Vote Act, the DISCLOSE Act, the Protecting Our Democracy Act, and the Ban Corporate PACs Act.
Even if we don't think we have the votes to overturn Citizens United, we should still try.
In the 16 years that we have had Citizens United go into effect, we see our airwaves, mailboxes, inboxes, and digital media influenced by all this money.
A lot of that is because of Citizens United.
I think the folks who spoke up today have really made a lot of good points about how many of us feel the anger of what is going on, but we are committed to getting this dark money out of politics.

It is disheartening to see some of the stories that we see every week about how foreign governments are influencing our policies now, and how foreign leaders, wealthy people, and wealthy corporations can easily buy some of our policymaking.
Then, you look at the 2012 cycle, after Citizens United: $231 million in spending.
There are a lot of issues right now that we can solve even without overturning Citizens United, although overturning Citizens United is our main goal.
There are more solutions that we can act on right now while we try to overturn Citizens United.
I introduced legislation, the Campaign and Election Accountability Act.
Mr. Speaker, I will definitely look into that bill.
